decisions.decision: Add smysl/1.0 to FORMAT_VERSIONS_SUPPORTED while keeping the writer on smysl/0.1.
decisions.rationale: Readers must be released before the writer is flipped so existing readers in the field do not reject output declaring the new version.
decisions.quote: §0.1 of ROAD_TO_1.0.md sequences that: readers learn `smysl/1.0` and are *released* first, and only a later cycle makes it what new documents say. Flip the writer before the field has a reader for it and every other implementation refuses the output — §8.2 requires a reader to reject a version absent from its list rather than guess.

decisions.decision: Defer making smysl/1.0 the default version that new documents declare.
decisions.rationale: The reader support in version 0.14 must first be published and adopted to prevent rejection by other implementations.
decisions.quote: Step 3 — making smysl/1.0 what new documents declare — waits for 0.14 to be published, because §8.2 requires a reader to refuse a version absent from its list: flip the writer before the field has a reader for it and every other implementation rejects the output.

decisions.rationale: The emitted format version and the accepted format versions no longer mean the same thing once multiple versions are supported.
decisions.quote: FORMAT_VERSION_DEFAULT is new and separate from FORMAT_VERSIONS_SUPPORTED[0], because the two stopped meaning the same thing the moment the list grew: one is what we emit, the other is what we accept.

decisions.decision: Preserve declared format version across parsing and surface writing.
decisions.rationale: Previously, the writer assumed FORMAT_VERSIONS_SUPPORTED[0], which would silently relabel documents declaring other supported versions upon formatting.
decisions.quote: ParseOutcome carries the version the document declared; WriteContext carries what the header will say; write_surface emits that instead of a build-time constant.

decisions.decision: Drive format version acceptance unit and integration tests from FORMAT_VERSIONS_SUPPORTED.
decisions.rationale: Hard-coded version checks caused tests to fail when smysl/1.0 was added because tests treated it as an example of an unknown version.
decisions.quote: All four are now driven by the list rather than by a literal, so they grow with it instead of failing on it.

decisions.decision: Decline updating version lists in python, nodejs, and go implementations.
decisions.rationale: Those implementations decode CBOR wire data only and never parse or see surface syntax @doc headers.
decisions.quote: The plan was wrong about the other three implementations. It said the same list grows in python/, nodejs/ and go/. There is no such list: all three read CBOR only, the wire carries no version string, and go/conformance_test.go says so outright — "surface syntax is not decoded here".

prerequisites.text: The specification requires readers to reject any document format version missing from their supported versions list.
prerequisites.quote: §8.2 requires a reader to refuse a version absent from its list: flip the writer before the field has a reader for it and every other implementation rejects the output.

prerequisites.text: A reader must refuse a document declaring a version missing from its supported version list.
prerequisites.quote: A reader must refuse a version absent from its list, so until 0.14 is on crates.io and in the field, a document declaring `smysl/1.0` is a document most readers reject.

prerequisites.text: ParseOutcome and WriteContext are non-exhaustive types, allowing non-breaking field additions.
prerequisites.quote: ParseOutcome and WriteContext are both #[non_exhaustive], so each could gain a field without a major bump and write_surface's signature never moved.

prerequisites.text: The CBOR wire format carries no format version string.
prerequisites.quote: The wire carries no version, so an implementation that reads only CBOR — `python/`, `nodejs/` and `go/` all do — has no version list to grow and nothing to change.

prerequisites.text: Tests were designed to fail automatically when the supported format version list expanded.
prerequisites.quote: versioning.rs was written in 0.10 to fail the moment the list grew, and it did — along with two sibling tests that had picked smysl/1.0 as their example of an *unknown* version

prerequisites.text: The Python, Node.js, and Go implementations only read CBOR wire data and do not parse surface syntax.
prerequisites.quote: all three read CBOR only, the wire carries no version string, and go/conformance_test.go says so outright — "surface syntax is not decoded here".

alternatives.alternative: Flipping the writer to smysl/1.0 before readers in the field are deployed.
alternatives.reason: Existing readers in the field reject any format version absent from their supported list.
alternatives.quote: Flip the writer before the field has a reader for it and every other implementation refuses the output

alternatives.alternative: Making smysl/1.0 the default emitted version immediately in release 0.14.
alternatives.reason: Un-upgraded readers in the field would reject documents declaring smysl/1.0 until 0.14 is adopted.
alternatives.quote: until 0.14 is on crates.io and in the field, a document declaring `smysl/1.0` is a document most readers reject.

alternatives.alternative: Continuing to rely on FORMAT_VERSIONS_SUPPORTED[0] for what the writer emits.
alternatives.reason: The emitted format version and accepted format versions diverge once multiple versions are supported.
alternatives.quote: the two stopped meaning the same thing the moment the list grew: the first is *what we emit*, the list is *what we accept*.

alternatives.alternative: Working around the defect and continuing to emit a build-time constant in write_surface.
alternatives.reason: Writing a build-time constant silently rewrites documents declaring a different supported version.
alternatives.quote: The defect the tripwire was guarding is fixed rather than worked around.

alternatives.alternative: Driving format version acceptance tests from literal version strings.
alternatives.reason: Literal checks fail when supported versions change instead of adapting alongside the supported list.
alternatives.quote: All four are now driven by the list rather than by a literal, so they grow with it instead of failing on it.

alternatives.alternative: Updating version lists across the python, nodejs, and go implementations.
alternatives.reason: Those implementations only decode CBOR wire data and do not have a surface syntax version list.
alternatives.quote: There is no such list: all three read CBOR only, the wire carries no version string

consequences.text: Documents declaring either supported version preserve their declared version across round-trip formatting.
consequences.quote: a document declaring either supported version comes back declaring the one it declared
consequences.verification_quote: Verified by restoring the old writer and watching it report "a document declaring `smysl/1.0` was rewritten as: @doc smysl/0.1".

consequences.text: ParseOutcome and WriteContext gained fields without introducing a breaking semver change.
consequences.quote: ParseOutcome and WriteContext are both #[non_exhaustive], so each could gain a field without a major bump

consequences.text: Tests adapt with FORMAT_VERSIONS_SUPPORTED instead of failing whenever the list expands.
consequences.quote: All four are now driven by the list rather than by a literal, so they grow with it instead of failing on it.

consequences.text: Migration work is reduced because non-Rust implementations do not process surface syntax headers.
consequences.quote: the migration is smaller than it looked
